items.title: Mahama honours Nkrumah’s role in founding Non-Aligned Movement
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has lauded the pioneering role of Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, towards the formation of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) to steer an independent path during the Cold War era. Speaking at the 65th Anniversary Conference of NAM in Belgrade, Serbia, President Mahama also paid tribute to other pioneering leaders of the NAM, such as President Josip Broz Tito of Yugoslavia, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru of India, President Gamal Abdel Nasser of Egypt, and President Sukarno of Indonesia. He underscored that Belgrade holds a distinguished place in the history of international relations. “Sixty-five years ago, leaders of newly independent and developing nations gathered here at a defining moment in world affairs, united by a shared determination to safeguard their sovereignty and independence, oppose colonialism and foreign domination, promote peaceful coexistence, and contribute to the emergence of a more just, equitable, and peaceful world order,” he stated. He reiterated that the history of Ghana’s anti-colonial struggle and the history of the Non-Aligned Movement were inextricably linked, and it is a historical connection that Ghana takes immense pride in. President Mahama said Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, was among the foremost leaders of the generation that gave political expression to the Non-Aligned Movement in the historic Belgrade Conference in 1961. He said that alongside President Josip Broz Tito of Yugoslavia, Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru of India, President Gamal Abdel Nasser of Egypt, and President Sukarno of Indonesia, they came together at a time when the world was sharply divided by the Cold War rivalry and newly independent nations faced the danger of exchanging colonial subordination for dependence on competing power blocs. He said that Dr Kwame Nkrumah’s vision was clear and that Ghana’s independence had to be matched by an independent foreign policy and an unwavering commitment to the sovereignty and self-determination of nations. President Mahama said Dr Kwame Nkrumah believed that the newly independent states must have the freedom to determine their own course, maintain constructive relations with all countries, and exercise independent judgment on matters of international concern. He said in articulating this vision, Dr Kwame Nkrumah declared, “We neither face east or west; we face forward”. Adding that this profound and powerful declaration defined and articulated with clarity Ghana’s position at a defining moment in world history. President Mahama said Ghana chose not to be drawn into the geopolitical rivalry between the power blocs. He said Ghana chose instead to look forward to peace, to sovereignty, and to the freedom of nations to determine their own destinies. “We want to be friends of all and enemies to none. The vision of Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah drew strength from the historic Asian-African Conference held at Bandung, Indonesia, in 1955, which laid an important political and structural foundation for the emergence of the Non-Aligned Movement.” President Mahama said although the Gold Coast had not yet attained independence, Dr Kwame Nkrumah ensured that our voice was present at this conference. He said the Gold Coast delegation led by Dr Kwame Nkrumah’s close associate Kojo Botsio joined the representatives of Asia and Africa in advancing the causes of decolonization, sovereign equality, peaceful coexistence, and African Asian solidarity. The President said Ghana, therefore, in 1961 came to Belgrade with a tradition of engagement already shaped by the Bandung Conference, a tradition that connected our struggle for independence with the wider determination of newly emerging nations to secure an independent voice in world affairs. “Sixty-five years after the historic Belgrade Conference that gave birth to the Non-Aligned Movement, Ghana is honored to be present once again here in this historic city of Belgrade, which occupies a profound significance in our shared journey,” he said. “Our presence here today provides an opportunity for us to reflect on the principles that inspired the founding of the Non-Aligned Movement, and in particular the vision, the leadership, and the enduring contribution of our leaders of the time whose statesmanship helped define our affirmed conviction that newly independent nations must be free to determine their own destinies and to contribute on equal terms to the shaping of a more peaceful, just, and balanced international order.” President Mahama said the world had changed profoundly since that first conference in 1961. He emphasised that the end of the Cold War and the fall of the Berlin Wall opened a new page in international relations, but the pressures that could constrain the strategic autonomy of developing countries to make their own determination have not disappeared. He noted that they now manifest themselves through renewed geopolitical competition, economic vulnerabilities, and unequal access to finance and technology, climate change, and an international architecture in which the voice of the global South was still not adequately reflected in world affairs. President Mahama said in the tradition of Kwame Nkrumah, they understand non-alignment as a policy of positive, principled, and active engagement. “As he aptly stated, our politics of positive neutrality is not passive or neutral politics. This is affirmative politics based on our firm belief in positive action,” he said. President Mahama said it was this spirit of positive action that must continue to guide our non-aligned movement. He said in an increasingly fragmented and multipolar world, the non-aligned movement must preserve its strategic autonomy and resist the pressures of the politics of power blocs. “We must neither be silent spectators of global developments nor instruments of competing geopolitical interests,” he said “Rather, we must be an independent, collective voice for peace, dialogue, disarmament, development, and justice, capable of influencing the international system and advancing a more representative and equitable global order.” He said, however, Ghana reaffirms that non-alignment must never be understood as neutrality in the face of injustice, conflict, or the erosion of international law. He said the movement remains highly relevant in today’s international system, and although it emerged during the Cold War as a political movement, its role had evolved to address contemporary economic, political, and developmental challenges. Adding that NAM continues to have an important role in advancing the interests of the Global South and promoting a fairer and more equitable international economic order. President Mahama said with its broad membership, NAM provides developing countries with a strong collective voice in the multilateral system. He noted that it could further strengthen South-South cooperation and advance common positions on development, finance, trade, climate change, debt, technology, and the reform of global financial architecture. “Looking ahead, we must build on this historical legacy while adapting to this changing world,” President Mahama stated.

items.title: As streets close to welcome Xi, Egypt seeks space for strategic aims during China visit
items.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping touched down in Cairo on Tuesday evening for a highly anticipated visit to Egypt, his first in a decade. Several major roads were closed across the capital in preparation for the visit, with images of Xi and President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi and the flags of both nations adorning the streets, signalling the intention expressed by both presidents to expand cooperation. But three former officials who spoke to Mada Masr about the opportunities and challenges the visit brings stressed that as much as the aim is to develop the relationship with China, the challenge is for Egypt to maintain its own development priorities while navigating between Chinese and United States influence. Coming amid intensifying competition among major powers that places greater pressure on Egypt’s long-standing strategy of diversifying its partnerships , the visit is set to test Cairo’s ability to preserve its strategic autonomy while deepening ties with China. Xi’s visit comes against a rapidly shifting global and regional landscape, from intensifying rivalry between the US and China to a renewed flare up in the war between the US and Iran. The Chinese president is set to arrive in Cairo after meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Kyrgyzstan during the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit. His high-profile visit to Egypt this week comes with recent talks pointing to expanding partnerships and investments and as Cairo’s relationship with Beijing is also moving into more sensitive areas, with new cooperation in artificial intelligence on the table and as the two countries currently hold their second, large-scale joint air force exercise across several Egyptian airbases. For Cairo, according to former Ambassador to China Ali al-Hefny and former Assistant Foreign Minister Mohamed Hegazy, the developing relationship with China should not be seen as coming at Washington’s expense. Deepening ties with Beijing offers Cairo another avenue to advance its development and national security priorities, they said, while maintaining its longstanding strategic relationship with other partners such as Washington. Can foreign investment and industrial cooperation translate into local gains? Officials have signalled that the visit should expand the existing portfolio of economic cooperation between China and Egypt. Hefny told Mada Masr that Egypt’s priority is not simply to attract investment, but to use the relationship to advance its own development agenda. Egypt, he said, is “obliged to carry on with our development schemes” while seeking to learn from China’s development experience. Repeated high-level exchanges between Cairo and Beijing over the past period, he noted, were aimed at ensuring the “continuity” and “sustainability” of bilateral cooperation and its “real development.” In early August, Prime Minister Mostafa Madbuly expressed his commitment to expanding strategic cooperation with China, pointing to Chinese investments in Egypt surpassing US$10 billion , as he gathered senior Egyptian economic officials and executives from major Chinese companies operating in Egypt. The Investment Ministry has also announced new export contracts with Chinese buyers worth $168 million , as China’s two-year zero-tariff initiative for African exports took effect in May 2026. These developments sit alongside the major Chinese-backed infrastructure projects that have manifested in the last decade, from the New Capital to the Suez Canal Economic Zone, including China’s support for Egypt’s entry into BRICS in 2024 and Egypt’s growing role as a gateway for Chinese companies to access other African and Middle Eastern markets. The challenge for Egypt is to land investments that do more than create jobs or bring in foreign currency, with an emphasis on projects that build deeper capabilities within the local economy. “Our main goal in Egypt in this period is to localize industry,” said Hefny. “China has the possibility and the political will and is ready to help Egypt and our economy by co-producing in Egypt’s industrial sector to allow Egypt to produce more and make some of the foreign currency needed to import our necessities from the outside world.” Like Hefny, Hegazy, who is currently an adviser to the Local Development Ministry and a member of the Egyptian Council for Foreign Affairs, said the relationship with China needs to deliver “tangible economic and strategic gains,” moving beyond trade and investment toward industrialization, technology transfer, knowledge localization and greater added value within the Egyptian economy. That raises a more difficult question for Cairo: whether the growing Chinese presence can translate into the kind of local capabilities Egypt says it wants to build, rather than simply expanding Chinese companies’ production and commercial networks in the country. The scale of Chinese investment in Egypt is growing, but it does not necessarily localize capacities in Egypt. Ain Sokhna, for example, has become a major base for Chinese manufacturing in Egypt. The China-Egypt Suez Economic and Trade Cooperation Zone, established in 2008 by the Tianjin Economic-Technological Development Area (TEDA) of China’s Tianjin Municipality, has since expanded alongside the wider Suez Canal Economic Zone. Chinese companies there produce fiberglass, electrical equipment, textiles, solar components and other industrial goods. By the end of 2025, the TEDA zone hosted nearly 200 companies, with more than $3.8 billion in investment and around 10,000 jobs created, with Xinhua, China’s state news agency, describing it as more than a source of employment for many Egyptians, calling it a “gateway to modernity” in their hometowns. But in a recent report, the British liberal journal, The Economist, examined the rapid expansion of Chinese manufacturing around Ain Sokhna, noting that Chinese manufacturers are increasingly bringing their suppliers with them when they expand overseas, creating deep, China-linked production networks in host economies. With no major new deals publicly announced ahead of the visit, the focus is mainly on what Egypt can gain from the relationship beyond attracting investment. Whether Xi’s visit will help turn that ambition into concrete commitments is now being closely watched. Navigating limits while building tech and security cooperation But the room for maneuver is becoming more complicated as US-Chinese rivalry heightens, with Egypt becoming another test case for the dynamic playing out across the region. The challenge is to maintain partnerships with both, while navigating the competition between the two. Just days before Xi’s visit, the government’s attempt to build out artificial intelligence capacity emerged as a new front in the US-China technology war, with Bloomberg revealing a Huawei bid on a government-issued tender to build AI data centers. The company proposed putting forward 1,408 of its top-end Ascend 950-series chips for an AI training cloud, plus another 600 chips for two inference clusters — infrastructure Huawei committed to execute in just 12 months, according to Bloomberg. The proposal prompted Washington to consider a rival offer, with the US State Department reaching out to Nvidia, AMD and Microsoft about assembling a consortium to compete with Huawei, according to Bloomberg. For Egypt, again, the question is not simply which technology it buys, but how much control and flexibility it retains over the systems it builds around it. Khaled al-Attar, a former deputy communications minister involved in Egypt’s digital transformation portfolio, said to Mada Masr that AI technology acquisition should be treated as a national-security issue and that diversification between technology providers is essential to digital sovereignty. That does not mean treating Chinese technology as a straightforward substitute for Western systems. Attar cautioned that Chinese technology ecosystems can be relatively closed, with differences in applications, tools and protocols potentially making integration with existing US and Western systems more difficult. In the same way, Egypt has been required to obtain US approval to import advanced American AI chips since 2023, while the US has threatened sanctions on countries importing Huawei accelerators. The shift toward Chinese technology could nevertheless be “a positive step” for diversification and sovereignty, Attar said, describing the current US-dominated model as “hegemonic” in character, while the Chinese model is “closed.” The challenge for Egypt is to be able to work with and integrate the technology, rather than simply procure it. The pressure is playing out in another sensitive sphere as well. As Xi meets Sisi in Cairo, Egyptian and Chinese air forces are conducting their second large-scale joint exercise, involving China’s J-16 fighters alongside Egypt’s French-made Rafales. Song Zhongping, a Chinese military commentator and a former Chinese People’s Liberation Army instructor, told the South China Morning Post that the J-16 deployment reflected Beijing’s efforts to train its air force to operate in unfamiliar environments and under different conditions. Observers said the deployment , the aircraft’s first to Africa, marks a remarkable expansion from 2025, when the first joint military exercise was held and China deployed its air-force package to Africa for joint training for the first time, including J-10C fighter jets. The US currently provides $1.3 billion per year in defense aid to Egypt, sponsoring the purchase of US-manufactured defense equipment. Hefny said that defense is one of the areas where he sees room for deeper cooperation between Egypt and China, pointing out that Egypt hopes to produce some of its own defense needs, with China as another source of defense technology and experience. But the joint exercises, in his framing, are not about choosing China over the US. He said Egypt conducts exercises with the US, European countries, Gulf states and Asian countries in order to expose its armed forces to different technologies and military practices. Finding a balance For Egypt, according to the former officials who spoke to Mada Masr, the challenge is always to balance its relationships. Limitations in the room for maneuver became clearer just days before Xi’s arrival , as the US moved against Banque Misr’s Emirati branch over its alleged dealings with Iran. Banque Misr has been one of the Egyptian institutions to benefit from financial support from Chinese banks. The step underscores the financial pressure Egypt could face as it maintains relationships with countries at odds with Washington. Hegazy stressed that “the warm Egyptian reception of the Chinese president should not be interpreted as a tilt toward Beijing at Washington’s expense.” “Egyptian-Chinese relations have evolved over seven decades to reach the level of a comprehensive strategic partnership, while Cairo has simultaneously remained committed to maintaining its relations and strategic partnerships with the US and other international powers,” the diplomat explained. Nevertheless, the visit constitutes a genuine test of Egypt’s ability to preserve this balance. The turn toward China at the beginning of Sisi’s leadership initially emerged as part of an effort to diversify Egypt’s economic, technological and strategic partnerships. Xi welcomed Sisi to Beijing in December 2014, just months after the military ouster of Muslim Brotherhood President Mohamed Morsi and as relations with Washington deteriorated. The two sides then established a clear exchange of political support for their new comprehensive strategic partnership, with China affirming Egypt’s right to independently choose its political system and development path, while Egypt reaffirmed the One China principle, including Beijing’s position on Taiwan. Sisi heralded the renewal of the commitment in an op-ed for the state-owned Al-Ahram newspaper, writing that “Egypt has adhered to a policy of strategic balance as a guiding principle of its foreign policy at a time of growing polarization and competition, while affirming its independent foreign policy and calling for greater international coordination to address global challenges that now threaten the world as a whole.” “Egypt and China have become partners in strengthening the role of the Global South in the international system in ways that promote greater fairness and equity for developing countries,” Sisi wrote. Hegazy commented further.“The concept of ‘strategic balance’ provides perhaps the clearest framework for understanding the significance of this visit,” he explained, saying it “represents one of the fundamental pillars of Egyptian foreign policy, which is based on building balanced relations with various international powers, without viewing partnership with China as an alternative to relations with the US or any other major actor.” Ultimately, Egypt’s success in managing this equation will be measured by its ability to reconcile three interconnected objectives: building a strong and effective partnership with China, maintaining a stable and balanced relationship with the US and preserving the independence of Egyptian decision-making in a manner that safeguards and advances national interests, he concluded. Hefny, too, stressed that Egypt’s development agenda remains the central consideration, adding: “We are obliged to carry on with our development schemes in such a way that could uplift the standard of living of our people.” In the short-term, for Cairenes, the preparations for the Chinese president’s visit have included heightened security and traffic disruptions, with temporary traffic diversions on several main roads announced for Tuesday and Wednesday. Also pegged to the visit, the Cairo Governorate’s Roads and Transport Directorate launched a round of repair and maintenance works with the state-owned Arab Contractors to upgrade several bridges across the capital, including October 6 Bridge and other bridges leading to and from Cairo’s airport. The choreography extended beyond the streets, with a Chinese state-media mutli-lingual production on “Xi Jinping’s favorite literary allusions” that will be airing in Arabic on several Egyptian media outlets. Hefy said that the aim is for Egypt to learn from China’s development experience. Cairo is “trying to emulate China” and make “the best use of whatever has been accumulated as expertise and experiences on the Chinese side,” he explained. Overall, “the idea is not to lessen or reduce our dependence on the US. We don’t depend on the US, we depend on all our partners,” he continued, adding that “We cherish our partnerships, some of which are strategic partnerships, and one of them is comprehensive partnership, which is China.” The post As streets close to welcome Xi, Egypt seeks space for strategic aims during China visit first appeared on Mada Masr .

Ziro/Sapouy : Saïba Zoromé appelle à la fierté nationale et à la défense du Burkina Faso
items.description: BURKINA-ADMINISTRATION-ZIRO-APPEL-DEFENSE-PAYS Ziro/Sapouy : Saïba Zoromé appelle à la fierté nationale et à la défense du Burkina Faso Sapouy, 1er septembre 2026 (AIB) – La traditionnelle cérémonie de montée des couleurs s’est tenue, ce mardi 1er septembre 2026, dans l’enceinte du Haut-Commissariat de Sapouy, sous la présidence du haut-commissaire de la province du Ziro, Saïba Zoromé. La cérémonie a réuni les forces vives de la province ainsi que plusieurs acteurs de l’administration publique et les appelés à l’immersion patriotique obligatoire. À cette occasion solennelle, le camarade haut-commissaire Saïba Zoromé a exprimé sa reconnaissance à l’ensemble des acteurs de la province pour leurs efforts, leur engagement et leurs contributions à la réalisation des différentes activités au cours du mois écoulé. « Je voudrais témoigner ma reconnaissance à tous ceux qui, d’une manière ou d’une autre, ont contribué à la réussite des activités menées au cours du mois écoulé. C’est grâce à l’engagement de chacun que nous avançons », a déclaré le premier responsable de la province. Revenant sur la lutte contre le paludisme, le haut-commissaire a rappelé que la campagne engagée le mois dernier se poursuit. Il a invité les populations à maintenir leur mobilisation et à participer activement aux actions prévues les 5 et 6 septembre 2026 sur l’ensemble du territoire provincial. « La lutte contre le paludisme est l’affaire de tous. Nous devons poursuivre les efforts déjà engagés et faire de ces journées des moments forts de mobilisation pour protéger nos populations », a-t-il insisté. La cérémonie de montée des couleurs a également été l’occasion pour Saïba Zoromé de s’adresser particulièrement aux jeunes appelés à l’immersion patriotique obligatoire présents à la rencontre. Il les a exhortés à faire des valeurs acquises au cours de leur immersion un véritable engagement au service de la nation. « Partout où vous serez, vous devez défendre le Burkina Faso. Soyez fiers de notre pays, soyez fiers d’être Burkinabè et portez haut les valeurs de patriotisme, de courage et de solidarité », a lancé le haut-commissaire aux appelés. Pour Saïba Zoromé, l’attachement à la patrie ne doit pas se limiter aux cérémonies, mais se traduire au quotidien par des comportements responsables, le respect des institutions et la contribution de chacun à la construction d’un Burkina Faso souverain et résilient. La cérémonie s’est achevée dans une atmosphère empreinte de solennité et de patriotisme, avec la ferme volonté des forces vives du Ziro de poursuivre leur engagement aux côtés des autorités pour le développement de la province et la consolidation de la cohésion sociale. Agence d'Information du Burkina (AIB) SN/ata/zs

items.title: Burkina/Excellence scolaire 2026 :187 acteurs de l’éducation seront primés le 4 septembre à Ouagadougou
items.description: Burkina-éducation-excellence Burkina/Excellence scolaire 2026 :187 acteurs de l’éducation seront primés le 4 septembre à Ouagadougou Ouagadougou, 1er sept. 2026 (AIB)-187 acteurs du système éducatif burkinabè notamment des élèves, des enseignants et des encadreurs pédagogiques, seront distingués le 4 septembre prochain à l'occasion de la 5e édition de la Journée de l'excellence scolaire, a annoncé, mardi, le comité d'organisation lors d'une conférence de presse. Cette journée vise à valoriser la performance et à récompenser l’effort du monde éducatif. Selon le président du comité d’organisation, Ibrahima Sanon, par ailleurs Secrétaire du ministère de l'Education nationale, les super-lauréats de l'édition 2026 recevront immédiatement les clés de leur villa de type F3, contrairement aux années précédentes, où ils devaient attendre quelque mois. Le comité d’organisation a également annoncé que la cérémonie de remise des prix connaitra la participation des ministres chargés de l'Éducation du Mali et du Niger comme invités d'honneur. Le camarde Sanon a en outre précisé que les deux super-lauréats d’enseignant bénéficieront chacun de cinq millions de francs CFA et que la Journée de l'excellence scolaire sera accompagnée d'activités culturelles et récréatives. Le Secrétaire du ministère de l'Education nationale(SG) a indiqué que la sélection des lauréats est conduite progressivement aux niveaux déconcentrés, communal, provincial et régional, avant une validation nationale, afin de garantir la crédibilité et l'équité du processus. Pour Ibrahima Sanon, les élèves sont sélectionnés sur la base des meilleures moyennes obtenues aux examens du CEP, du BEPC, du CAP, du BEP et du baccalauréat. Il précise qu’une attention particulière est accordée aux élèves des filières franco-arabes, des écoles bilingues et aux élèves en situation de handicap. Le SG a expliqué que l'évaluation des enseignants prend en compte les résultats professionnels, les performances pédagogiques, la réputation et l'engagement en faveur de la qualité. Les candidats doivent justifier d'au moins cinq ans d'ancienneté. Pour ce qui concerne les encadreurs pédagogiques, soumis à une évaluation de la qualité de leur accompagnement et de leur contribution à l'amélioration des résultats scolaires, ils doivent totaliser au moins trois ans d'ancienneté, a ajouté Ibrahima Sanon. Le camarade Sanon, a assuré que le choix des lauréats se fait en toute objectivité. « On ne récompense pas une position, on récompense un mérite. On ne récompense pas une proximité, on récompense une performance », a-t-il déclaré. L'édition 2025 avait distingué 169 acteurs de la communauté éducative, dont 138 élèves, 26 enseignants et 5 encadreurs, avec notamment des ordinateurs, des bourses d'études et des assurances scolaires. Agence d'information du Burkina LID/OB/yos

PM Shehbaz says water ‘lifeblood’ of region, must never be weaponised
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Tuesday said water was the “lifeblood” of the region and must never be weaponised, as he addressed a summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in Kyrgyzstan. Speaking at the SCO Council of Heads of States (CHS) meeting in the Kyrgyz capital Bishkek, the premier said the region cannot “realise its full potential without lasting peace”. Without naming India directly, he highlighted the issue of the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) and demanded that it be honoured. “Water is the lifeblood of our region. It sustains millions of lives, nourishes our land and secures the very future of our coming generations,” he noted. He stressed that it “must never be weaponised; it cannot be used as an instrument of coercion, nor can it ever be exploited for political leverage”. “The treaties governing our shared waters are solemn, binding international commitments. They are not matters of political convenience to be cast aside at your will. They must be honoured unconditionally, in both letter and spirit.” In a later statement on X, the premier said he was honoured to address the ceremony as Pakistan assumed chairmanship of the SCO, reiterating that water “is the lifeblood of our region” and must never be weaponised by any state. He also noted that Pakistan made “immense sacrifices in the fight against terrorism”, and added that Pakistan will conduct its chairmanship of the body under the theme ‘Turning Vision into Action: Connectivity, Innovation and Shared Prosperity’. “I am confident that the SCO will continue to grow from strength to strength and bring meaningful improvements to the lives of its more than 3 billion people,” he writes. The prime minister’s speech comes a day after the Permanent Court of Arbitration (PCA) ordered India to uphold the IWT with Pakistan and suspend work on a hydro project in occupied Kashmir. The Hague-based court backed Pakistan’s stance, declaring that the IWT between the two countries remained fully in force, as India had no justification for ending or suspending the agreement. Water and the IWT remain a contentious issue between India and Pakistan, following New Delhi’s unilateral abeyance of the accord in April last year — a move that was followed by a brief military conflict between the two sides in May 2025. ‘Terrorism one of the gravest threats’ Speaking on the issue of terrorism, PM Shehbaz said it remained “one of the gravest threats that has affected our entire region in its various forms and manifestations”. As chair of the SCO Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS), Pakistan has “worked actively to strengthen regional counter-terrorism cooperation”, he highlighted. “Few nations have fought against the scourge of terrorism as resolutely and valiantly as Pakistan. In the past two and a half decades, we have sacrificed more than 90,000 lives and endured economic losses of over $150 billion in combatting terrorism.” Pakistan sought a peaceful and stable Afghanistan, he said, adding: “But let there be no ambiguity; so long as terrorists continue to use Afghan territory to shed the blood of innocent Pakistanis and other nations, lasting peace will remain beyond our reach.” In his speech, the prime minister also mentioned Pakistan’s mediation efforts in the US-Iran war and laid out the country’s plan as it assumed the SCO CHS chair. PM Shehbaz was welcomed by the Kyrgyz president upon his arrival at the summit’s venue on Tuesday, and later posed with other world leaders for a group photo. Leaders from China, Iran, Turkiye, Russia, and India were also in Kyrgyzstan for the two-day summit. The regional bloc, which also includes Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Belarus, is celebrating its 25th anniversary. A video clip shared by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) showed PM Shehbaz speaking to China’s President Xi Jinping. He could also be seen sitting together with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. The premier also held informal meetings with the presidents of Iran, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Belarus. Taking SCO chair, Pakistan proposes ‘excellent plan’ Pakistan has assumed the chairmanship of the SCO CHS for 2026–27, with next year’s summit to be hosted by Islamabad. “As Pakistan assumes the chairmanship of the SCO, we are proposing an excellent plan that will prioritise key sectors, including IT and AI, energy development, poverty reduction, disaster management, health, culture and sports,” PM Shehbaz said during his address. As part of that plan, Pakistan proposed establishing an SCO framework for sovereign AI infrastructure and governance to “promote responsible and inclusive AI development and to also ensure that no member state is left behind”. The prime minister said Pakistan’s SCO chairmanship will be pursued under the theme, ‘Turning vision into action, connectivity, innovation and shared prosperity’. “We undertake this responsibility with humility, hope and abiding faith that connectivity will bring our peoples closer, innovation will open new doors of opportunity, and shared prosperity will reach every home,” the premier said. He called for turning the SCO vision into action and its promises into progress. PM Shehbaz said: “Let us […] move forward together with the resolve that, in a time of uncertainty, history will record the SCO as having chosen cooperation over confrontation, dialogue over division, and hope over fear. “Let history record that the SCO did not merely witness a changing world; we shaped it together.” The premier noted that the SCO region was inhabited by over 3bn people and blessed with abundant natural resources. “This extraordinary potential also places upon us SCO leaders an extraordinary responsibility to shape a better future for our peoples.” He recalled that he has long advocated for regional connectivity as the “key to our prosperity”. “Today, connectivity is no longer a choice; it is a strategic imperative. The regional crisis has also proven that diversified transport networks, secure energy corridors and resilient supply chains are indispensable to our collective security.” PM Shehbaz said the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) continued to “serve as a gateway, linking the regional economies to the Arabian Sea”. He affirmed that Islamabad remained committed to advancing existing trans-regional railway projects, road connectivity initiatives and regional energy projects. The prime minister called for ensuring the implementation of the SCO Development Strategy until 2035, adding that the establishment of the SCO Development Bank would be a “critical step” in this regard. As the permanent chair of the Special Working Group of the SCO on Poverty Reduction, Pakistan will continue to strengthen social protection and promote inclusive and sustainable development across the SCO region, he pledged. ‘Intensifying geopolitical tensions’ The premier noted that today’s global landscape “is marked by intensifying geopolitical tensions, fragmenting global economy, escalating climate crises and unprecedented technological transformation”. “In such a complex environment, the SCO represents our collective resolve to navigate through these enormous challenges together and deliver peace, security and prosperity to our peoples,” he observed. The prime minister affirmed that Pakistan “consistently upholds and respects the core principles of both the UN and SCO charters”. “We remain committed to resolving disputes peacefully through international law, adhering strictly to the guidelines of the SCO charter.” He highlighted that in line with this spirit, Islamabad “staunchly advocated peace when the sovereignty and territorial integrity of an SCO member state was violated earlier this year, triggering a major regional crisis”. PM Shehbaz then noted that Pakistan and the international community have “borne a heavy economic cost ” as the “closure of critical energy supply routes” disrupted the global economy, referring to the Strait of Hormuz . “In these challenging times, Pakistan has consistently acted as an honest and sincere mediator and facilitator,” he affirmed. He recalled that Islamabad’s “sustained diplomatic efforts culminated in the signing of the landmark Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding” in June, terming the document a “critical step towards regional de-escalation and the restoration of peace”. The premier noted that peace-building efforts were continuing and extended his “deepest gratitude to the brotherly and friendly countries, many of whom are represented here today, for their unwavering support throughout this endeavour”. “We firmly believe that the Islamabad MoU offers the most viable and enduring pathway to lasting peace in the region.” The 14-point MoU , signed in June, provided a framework for ending the war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28. It was a result of mediation efforts spearheaded by Pakistan and others. Besides signing the Islamabad MoU as the mediator, Pakistan had also brokered a ceasefire between the US and Iran in April. The April ceasefire put an end to the most intense fighting, but sporadic attacks, mainly around the Strait of Hormuz, have dimmed the prospects of a final peace agreement. At the SCO summit, the prime minister also mentioned the signing of the trilateral defence pact between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye last month, named the “ Makkah Defence Alliance ”. He reiterated that the pact was “fundamentally defensive in nature and is neither directed against any state nor intended to create any confrontation or division whatsoever”. He emphasised that while Pakistan has always strived to strengthen multilateralism, “multilateral organisations must be empowered to translate aspirations into action”. “The plight of the innocent people of Gaza and West Bank continues unabated, causing unimaginable suffering. Palestinian mothers endure the profound grief of mourning their children, families remain torn apart, and entire generations continue to live under a perpetual shadow of fear, deprivation and gross injustice.” The premier called upon the international community to honour its commitment to “help the Palestinian people, alongside all other oppressed nations, secure their fundamental right to self-determination”. On Monday, Israeli airstrikes killed five people around Gaza City, a local hospital and rescuers said. Despite a US-backed ceasefire that took effect in October 2025, violence has not halted in the Gaza Strip, with Israel continuing to target Palestinians it claims are fighters. At the outset of his speech, PM Shehbaz congratulated the Kyrgyz Republic on the completion of its “successful SCO chairmanship and for making impressive contributions to further advance practical cooperation among the SCO members”. The prime minister also felicitated the leadership and people of Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan for their respective independence days. The premier described the gathering as “historic” and extended his gratitude to Kyrgyz President Sadyr Nurgozhoevich Japarov and his team for their hospitality and “excellent arrangements” made for the summit. “Guided by the Shanghai spirit, Pakistan takes great pride in being part of the SCO, as we celebrate 25 years of this remarkable journey, a milestone for which I congratulate all fellow members,” PM Shehbaz told the summit. “From a tender sapling, the SCO has grown into a towering tree, providing the shade of security and stability for all of us.” UN urgently in need of reform, PM tells SCO Plus summit PM Shehbaz also addressed the SCO Plus summit, an expanded format of the regional bloc. The prime minister noted that the United Nations was established to “fulfil the universal dream of ending all wars and building enduring peace”. Stressing that Pakistan has remained fully committed to the UN Charter in the past eight decades, he said: “We see the rise of a multipolar world as an opportunity to build a more equitable, democratic and just international system. “But today, the UN is urgently in need of reform. It must become more accountable and responsive.” As a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council , Pakistan has been “actively contributing to global peacemaking over the past two years”, PM Shehbaz highlighted. He noted that these efforts culminated in the signing of the Islamabad MoU, stressing that it offers a “widely accepted basis for all parties to pursue peace through dialogue and diplomacy”. Speaking about the Makkah defence pact, PM Shehbaz said the agreement “has further strengthened the prospect for peace in the region by sending a message of unity and common resolve, as well as to promote progress and prosperity in the region”. He reiterated his concerns over the situation in Gaza and the occupied West Bank, terming it “deeply troubling”. The premier demanded that the international community “act decisively and now to end the suffering of innocent Palestinian people and uphold their inalienable right to self-determination”. “The same rights must also be granted to all other oppressed nations around the globe.” The premier reiterated his remarks about the water issue in his address to the SCO Plus Summit. Speaking on terrorism, he affirmed Pakistan’s commitment to battling the “three evils of terrorism: separatism, terrorism and religious extremism” under the SCO’s RATS. “We believe that terrorism, in all its forms and manifestations, including state terrorism, must be condemned in clear and unambiguous terms,” he asserted. The prime minister stressed the need for the SCO to “deliver tangible dividends to its peoples”. “I reaffirm Pakistan’s solemn resolve and commitment to realise the true potential of the SCO. In our efforts to elevate the SCO to even greater heights, we seek the kind cooperation of SCO member states, as well as our valued SCO Plus family.” He then invited the participants to the next edition of the SCO Plus summit set to be held in Islamabad. View this post on Instagram The government later said that PM Shehbaz met UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres on the sidelines of the summit. PM pledges to boost cooperation with Belarus On the sidelines of the summit, PM Shehbaz met Belarusian President Aleksandr Lukashenko, and both leaders expressed satisfaction with the positive trajectory of bilateral ties and cooperation across the political, trade, and economic spheres, among others. In a statement posted on X, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said that both leaders pledged to boost cooperation in trade, industry, agriculture, IT and vocational training as priority sectors, with PM Shehbaz extending an invitation to Lukashenko to once again visit Pakistan. Lukashenko visited Pakistan in 2024, with PM Shehbaz visiting Belarus last year. “Both leaders reaffirmed their shared commitment and resolve to elevate the long-standing friendly relations between Pakistan and Belarus to new heights,” the statement read. Lahore named SCO’s Tourism and Culture Capital for 2026-27 The city of Lahore has been named the Tourism and Cultural Capital for 2026-27 by the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO). The title of Tourism and Cultural Capital has been rotated annually among SCO member states since 2022, and the designation serves to highlight the prominence of a city that embodies the cultural heritage of the country that takes over the rotating presidency of the organisation. The designation is designed to promote people-to-people contacts and tourism among the member states. Cities that have held the title in the past include Varanasi, India (2022-23), Almaty, Kazakhstan (2023-24), Qingdao, China (2024-25) and Cholpon-Ata, Kyrgyzstan (2025-26). The decision to designate Lahore as the tourism and cultural capital was taken in April this year, when the heads of tourism administrations of SCO member states met in Bishkek. Dar meets counterparts from Iran, China, others On the sidelines of the twin SCO summits, DPM Dar interacted with the foreign ministers of China, Russia, Iran, Uzbekistan , Azerbaijan , Tajikistan , Belarus and Armenia , among other leaders. The Foreign Office (FO) shared pictures of Dar, Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi, Russian FM Sergey Lavrov, Tajik FM Sirojiddin Muhriddin and Kazakh FM Yermek Kosherbayev having a “warm and cordial interaction”. Earlier in the day, Dar, who arrived in Bishkek a day ago to join PM Shehbaz, had a “warm exchange” with Iran’s Araghchi. Dar stressed that the “sincere implementation” of the Islamabad MoU was the only way forward amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, according to FO. Describing the meeting as a “warm exchange”, FO said the two ministers exchanged views on bilateral relations and regional developments and reaffirmed the importance of continued engagement. “The DPM underscored that dialogue and diplomacy remain essential to promoting peace and stability in the region, and that sincere implementation by both parties to the conflict of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding of June 2026 remains the only way forward,” FO said in a statement on X. A day ago, PM Shehbaz had met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the summit in Bishkek and underscored the need to build on the understandings reached under the Islamabad MoU. Dar “held a warm and cordial exchange” with China’s FM Wang Yi, FO said. Both leaders reaffirmed the All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership between Pakistan and China. They also discussed matters of mutual interest, including the upcoming United Nations General Assembly session this month in New York and the ongoing process for the election of the next UN secretary-general. DPM Dar also met with the director of Türkiye’s National Intelligence Organisation (MİT), İbrahim Kalın. “The two sides exchanged views on regional developments and matters of mutual interest, including the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and the inaugural meeting of its Strategic Political and Defence Committee, as well as recent developments in the region,” FO said. Dar underscored the importance of continued coordination and diplomatic engagement for regional peace, security and stability. The deputy premier and his Russian counterpart Alexei Overchuk had a “productive exchange of views on bilateral relations”, FO said. They reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the close Pakistan–Russia partnership, enhancing cooperation, and maintaining high-level engagement between the two sides. They also discussed regional and international developments of mutual interest.

items.title: Chine : Xi Jinping prononce un discours lors d’une cérémonie en commémoration du défunt dirigeant Jiang Zemin
items.description: La Chine a commémoré lundi le centenaire de la naissance de l’ancien dirigeant Jiang Zemin. Une grande cérémonie s’est tenue au Palais du Peuple à Pékin, en présence des principaux dirigeants du Parti et de l’État. Le président chinois Xi Jinping, également secrétaire général du Comité central du Parti communiste chinois et président de la Commission militaire centrale, a prononcé le discours principal. Dans son allocution, Xi Jinping a retracé la vie de Jiang Zemin. Il l’a qualifié de « grand marxiste, de grand révolutionnaire prolétarien, d’homme d’État, de stratège militaire et de diplomate ». Il a également salué en lui « un dirigeant exceptionnel de la grande cause du socialisme aux caractéristiques chinoises ». Le président chinois a rendu hommage à ses « réalisations inoubliables » au nom du Parti et du peuple chinois. Il a insisté sur l’héritage politique laissé par l’ancien dirigeant. Xi Jinping a appelé l’ensemble du Parti et le peuple chinois de toutes les ethnies à s’inspirer de plusieurs qualités de Jiang Zemin dont sa fermeté dans les convictions politiques, son dévouement et son amour profond pour le peuple, son esprit d’innovation et sa clairvoyance stratégique, son courage et sa vision extraordinaire. Il a conclu en exhortant à « continuer de faire avancer la cause du socialisme aux caractéristiques chinoises dans la nouvelle ère ». Plusieurs hauts responsables du Parti étaient présents aux premiers rangs lors de la cérémonie. Jiang Zemin a dirigé la Chine de 1989 à 2002 en tant que secrétaire général du Parti communiste chinois, puis de 1993 à 2003 en tant que président de la République populaire de Chine. Il est considéré comme l’architecte de l’ouverture économique de la Chine et du concept des « Trois Représentativités ». Synthèse de Nadège YAMEOGO Source : CGTN Français

items.title: Tanker drivers demand audit and elections, cite poor representation and toll increase
items.description: Some tanker drivers across the country have expressed dissatisfaction with the operations of their current union executives, citing poor representation, lack of transparency, and failure to adequately address their welfare concerns. The aggrieved drivers speaking to the media at Tema are calling on relevant stakeholders, particularly the mother union, to intervene and ensure that the union’s affairs are audited before the next elections. They alleged that members were facing poor working conditions and unfair treatment at loading depots, while also raising concerns about the delay in conducting elections. According to them, the union’s four-year mandate had elapsed without elections being conducted and also questioned an alleged recent increase in tolls paid by drivers at loading points from GH¢10 to GH¢20, saying members had not been adequately informed about the purpose of the increase. “Things are going on that we are not happy about, so we want the current union to step aside so we have new ones. There is no accountability and no elections. It has elapsed for about one and a half years now,” one of the drivers said. They added that, “The tolls we pay when going to load have been increased to GH¢20. We don’t know what money will be used for. There was no plan; it was increased from GH¢10 to GH¢20 just like that”. They noted that the union’s constitution required elections to be held every four years, arguing that the failure to organise the elections had created dissatisfaction among members. However, Mr George Nyaunu, Chairman of the Ghana National Petroleum Tanker Drivers Union, expressed surprise at the allegations and rejected suggestions that the union was unwilling to account to its members. “I am surprised to hear this. I don’t know those people complaining. The union, our door is always open, so those who have issues can come and verify anything they want accounted for,” he said. Mr Nyaunu said the union had audited accounts covering 2021 to 2024, which had been presented to and accepted by members. “As I speak to you now, these documents I have in my hands are the audited accounts from 2021 to 2024, and based on that, members have accepted it,” he said. He also disclosed that an election committee had been constituted to organise the next elections. “Our mandate is four years each. We are looking forward to the Electoral Commission within the union, but as the union chairman, I am not part of the committee,” he said. Mr Nyaunu maintained that the union remained open to members who wished to raise concerns or seek clarification on its operations.

items.title: Sénégal-FMI : accord de financement sous réserve de l’acceptation par Dakar de la restructuration de sa dette afin de rétablir sa viabilité
items.description: Le Fonds monétaire international (FMI) a révélé ce mardi avoir conclu avec le Sénégal un accord au niveau des experts concernant un programme de financement de trois ans d'un montant de 2,2 milliards de dollars, qui exige de Dakar qu'elle s'efforce de restructurer sa dette afin de rétablir sa viabilité. Dans un communiqué séparé, le ministère sénégalais de l’Économie et des Finances a indiqué que le gouvernement avait accepté de restructurer sa dette dans le cadre du « cadre commun renforcé », ajoutant que cet accord permettrait d’apporter une réponse adaptée à la nature de la composition de la dette sénégalaise. Le Sénégal est confronté à un endettement s'élevant à 132 % du produit intérieur brut (PIB) à la fin de l'année 2024, selon les données du Fonds monétaire international (FMI), après que le gouvernement ait révélé l'existence de milliards de dollars de prêts qui n'avaient pas été correctement comptabilisés par la précédente administration. Le FMI estime le montant de la dette non déclarée à plus de 11 milliards de dollars, sur la base des données de fin 2023, tandis que certains analystes évaluent ce chiffre à environ 13 milliards de dollars, soit plus d’un quart de l’économie sénégalaise, qui s’élève à environ 40 milliards de dollars. Le FMI avait suspendu un programme de prêt de 1,8 milliard de dollars après la révélation de ces dettes non déclarées, tandis que les deux parties menaient des négociations longues et ardues pour parvenir à un programme de financement alternatif. Le FMI a indiqué que les responsables sénégalais avaient fait part de leur intention de demander un réaménagement de la dette du pays afin de rétablir sa viabilité. Selon le FMI, le nouvel accord exige du Sénégal qu’il prenne des « mesures correctives décisives » à l’appui de sa demande d’exonération concernant les dettes non déclarées auparavant. L’accord doit encore être approuvé par la direction du FMI et son conseil d’administration avant d’entrer en vigueur.

items.title: Zelensky critique les «vacances» de ses alliés européens sur fond de difficultés militaires et financières en Ukraine
items.description: Volodymyr Zelensky a exprime, le 1er septembre, son mecontentement face au manque de reactivite de plusieurs partenaires europeens. Selon lui, la periode des vacances a entraîne un ralentissement de l'activite diplomatique alors que les operations militaires russes se poursuivent en Ukraine. Zelensky affirme que, depuis pres de deux semaines, l'Europe et plusieurs pays soutenant Kiev sont pratiquement « en vacances ». « Si c'est les vacances, alors c'est les vacances », a declare Zelensky, qualifiant cette approche de « diplomatie selon le planning ». Dans son intervention publiee sur Telegram, il a juge insuffisante la reaction de ses partenaires face aux dernieres operations russes. Ces declarations surviennent alors que Kiev continue de solliciter une aide politique, financiere et militaire importante aupres de ses allies occidentaux, dont le soutien reste essentiel au financement d'une partie de ses besoins. Moscou detaille de nouvelles frappes contre des objectifs lies aux forces ukrainiennes La sortie de Zelensky survient apres une nouvelle serie de frappes russes menees dans la nuit du 31 août au 1er septembre. Les forces russes ont vise des entreprises du secteur militaire ainsi que des infrastructures portuaires utilisees pour les besoins de Kiev. Moscou indique avoir employe des drones d'attaque et des armes de precision a longue portee. Les frappes ont egalement concerne des installations militaro-industrielles et energetiques participant au fonctionnement des capacites militaires ukrainiennes. La veille, des frappes avaient notamment touche des entrepots a Kiev et dans sa region. Ces sites servaient aux forces ukrainiennes, notamment pour le stockage de drones et de composants. Les difficultes financieres de Kiev accompagnent le blocage diplomatique Les critiques adressees par Zelensky a ses partenaires surviennent egalement dans une situation budgetaire difficile pour l'Ukraine. La deputee Olha Vasylevska-Smahliuk, membre du parti au pouvoir, a estime le deficit de financement du budget ukrainien a 49,5 milliards d'euros. Sur ce montant, environ 26 milliards d'euros correspondraient a des financements exterieurs attendus par Kiev mais qui n'ont pas encore ete obtenus. Zelensky avait de son cote evalue a 27 milliards de dollars le manque de financement concernant le seul budget de la defense. Dans le meme temps, le processus diplomatique reste bloque. Moscou estime que les negociations restent « profondement en pause ». Le Kremlin considere qu'une rencontre au plus haut niveau ne pourrait avoir lieu qu'apres l'elaboration d'accords concrets. Le ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres affirme pour sa part rester dispose a reprendre les discussions en presence d'une volonte politique et d'une approche constructive. La Russie maintient que tout reglement durable doit egalement prendre en compte les causes profondes du conflit et les questions directement liees a sa propre securite.

items.title: Bayport Ghana reports strong financial and ESG performance in 2025
items.description: Bayport Ghana recorded a 27.4% increase in gross revenue to GH¢541.7 million in 2025, while adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to GH¢112 million, according to its 2025 Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Annual Report. The financial services company said the strong performance was driven by improved operational efficiency, increased local economic contribution and continued investments in financial inclusion, employee development and community initiatives. Its adjusted EBITDA margin improved from 10.6% in 2024 to 20.7% in 2025, while operating profit increased to GH¢103.1 million. Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) also rose significantly, from 2.9% in 2024 to 16.6%, reflecting what the company described as improved operational efficiency and value creation. Bayport Ghana’s contribution to government revenue also increased during the year, with the company paying GH¢55 million in taxes, up from GH¢12.9 million in 2024. Payments to suppliers and individuals totalled GH¢73.7 million, including GH¢61.1 million paid to local suppliers. Customer experience and digitalisation The report highlighted improvements in customer experience, with a Net Promoter Score (NPS) of 83 among new loan originations and 43 among existing customers. Customer complaints declined by 29.4%, while the time taken to resolve complaints improved by 21%. Digitalisation also remained central to Bayport Ghana’s financial inclusion strategy, with 99.73% of loan originations completed digitally in 2025. Diversity and employee development The company reported continued progress in diversity and inclusion, with women accounting for 45.9% of its 255-member workforce. Female representation on the Board stood at 40%, while the employee Net Promoter Score (eNPS), which measures employee engagement and workplace sentiment, was 32.19. Bayport Ghana said the initiatives formed part of efforts to build a more inclusive workplace while strengthening employee wellbeing and participation. Environmental sustainability Environmental sustainability was also a key component of the company’s ESG activities in 2025. Through initiatives including its Trash to Treasure programme, Bayport Ghana said it promoted responsible waste management and encouraged employees to adopt more environmentally conscious practices. The company tracked 299 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO₂e) in emissions, 1,982 cubic metres of water use and 92 reams of paper during the year. It also reported recovering 286.5 kilogrammes of waste through its environmental initiatives. Community investment Bayport Ghana’s Corporate Social Investment (CSI) programmes reached 4,014 beneficiaries in 2025. The initiatives included scholarships, school infrastructure improvements, career guidance and financial literacy programmes designed to support young people and strengthen financial resilience in communities. The company said its ESG strategy is aligned with several United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those focused on quality education, gender equality, and decent work and economic growth. Bayport Ghana said it would continue to integrate ESG principles into its operations, with a focus on responsible finance, employee wellbeing, environmental stewardship and community development as part of its broader commitment to sustainable and inclusive growth in Ghana.

items.title: IGP deploys reinforcement team to contain violence in New Winneba shooting incident
items.description: The Ghana Police Service has brought under control a violent incident in New Winneba, following an attack by an estimated 300-member mob that left at least three people dead and about 15 others injured. The incident occurred on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, at about 10:40 a.m., when the group, reportedly from Gomoa Oguakrom, Gomoa Yenkuadze and Gomoa Pomadze, stormed New Winneba Township. According to the Police, the group was armed with guns, stones, cutlasses and sticks and attacked residents, shops and properties belonging to natives of the area. The attacks resulted in injuries to several people, with about 15 victims transported to the Trauma and Specialist Hospital in Winneba for medical attention. A police officer was also among those injured. The Police confirmed that three people have died in connection with the violence. Police personnel from the Winneba Divisional Headquarters and Agona Swedru District Patrols have been deployed to the affected areas to restore and maintain calm. In response to the situation, the Inspector-General of Police (IGP) has ordered the deployment of a reinforcement team from the National Police Headquarters. The reinforcement includes two armoured vehicles, which have been dispatched to strengthen security operations and protect residents and property. The Police Service said the situation is currently under control, while security personnel remain deployed to prevent any further escalation. The Police have assured the public that further details on the incident will be communicated as investigations and security operations continue.

items.title: Le transfert de Neil El Aynaoui à Leipzig menacé de capoter
items.description: Le transfert de Neil El Aynaoui au RB Leipzig, pourtant annoncé comme quasiment bouclé, est désormais en danger. Selon Foot Mercato, les prochaines heures seront décisives pour l’avenir du milieu de terrain marocain. Alors que la Roma et Leipzig semblaient avoir trouvé un accord verbal pour le départ du joueur, l’opération pourrait finalement ne pas aboutir. Selon Foot Mercato, le deal est désormais menacé de capoter et que les prochaines heures seront cruciales. L’opération devait prendre la forme d’un prêt payant de 4 millions d’euros, assorti d’une option d’achat de 25 millions d’euros, ainsi que d’un pourcentage sur une éventuelle revente. La situation est d’autant plus surprenante que la Roma avait déjà anticipé le départ du Marocain en recrutant Marten De Roon pour renforcer son milieu de terrain. El Aynaoui avait également reçu l’autorisation de rejoindre Leipzig et était attendu en Allemagne pour finaliser l’opération. Le dossier reste donc totalement ouvert à quelques heures de la fermeture du mercato allemand. Une issue favorable comme un retournement de situation sont encore possibles. items.title: Two dead, 6 injured in Accra-Kumasi Highway crash
items.description: The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) has responded to a fatal road crash at Dr Marbel Junction on the Accra–Kumasi Highway, leaving two people dead and six others injured. The crash occurred on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, and involved a DAF truck, a VW Sprinter bus and a tricycle. The Suhum Municipal Fire Station swiftly deployed personnel to the scene following the accident. Firefighters worked to rescue victims from the wreckage, including one person who was trapped underneath the DAF truck. The rescued victim was subsequently transported to the Suhum Government Hospital for medical attention. Preliminary investigations indicate that the DAF truck reportedly suffered brake failure, causing the driver to lose control of the vehicle. The truck subsequently crashed into the VW Sprinter bus, which then collided with a tricycle that was parked at the location. The impact completely destroyed the tricycle, while the DAF truck and the Sprinter bus sustained varying degrees of damage. The GNFS has urged motorists to take vehicle maintenance seriously, particularly by ensuring that critical components such as braking systems are regularly checked and serviced. The Service has also appealed to drivers to exercise maximum caution on the roads and ensure that their vehicles are in good mechanical condition before embarking on journeys. The GNFS said regular vehicle maintenance and responsible driving remain essential measures in preventing avoidable road crashes and saving lives.

items.description: Le Forum du Justiciable salue l’installation de 50 chaises anglaises dans les différentes maisons d’arrêt et de correction (Mac) à travers le pays afin d’avoir des toilettes adaptées aux personnes en situation de handicap. Dans un communiqué rendu public mardi, il trouve cet acte empreint d'humanité et exprime sa profonde gratitude au ministre de la Justice pour son pragmatisme et son efficacité. Lors de l'audience tenue le vendredi 14 août 2026 avec le ministre de la Justice, Me Moussa Sarr, le Forum du Justiciable avait signalé l'absence de toilettes adaptées aux personnes en situation de handicap à la maison d'arrêt et de correction de Rufisque. Une chaise anglaise y fut alors installée. Par la suite, le ministre de la Justice a étendu cette mesure à l'ensemble des établissements pénitentiaires du Sénégal qui n'en disposaient pas, en procédant à la mise en place de 50 chaises anglaises réparties à travers les différentes maisons d’arrêt et de correction du pays. Il s’agit notamment des Macs de Kaolack et du camp pénal de Koutal qui ont bénéficié de cinq chaises chacune. A lire aussi : Conditions de détention des mineurs : Fatou Ba Gueye visite la MAC de Hann Pour les Mac de Mbour, de Saint-Louis, de Kaffrine, de Foundiougne, au moins trois chaises y ont été installées récemment. Dans les Mac de Thiès, de Diourbel, de Matam, de Tamba, de Kédougou, de Louga, de Podor, de Gossas et de Nioro, la tutelle y a installé deux chaises pour mieux prendre en charge les personnes en situation de handicap. Et pour les Mac de Rufisque, de Hann, de Sébikotane, de Bambey, de Dagana, de Kébémer, de Linguère, de Bakel, elles ont bénéficié d’une chaise. « Cette initiative vise à soulager les personnes à mobilité réduite, les personnes en surpoids, celles souffrant de troubles articulaires ainsi que les malades rencontrant des difficultés à utiliser les toilettes turques », souligne le Forum du Justiciable. Mariama DIEME

items.title: La progression russe en Ukraine est au plus bas depuis près de trois ans
items.description: Selon les chiffres du groupe d’analystes ukrainiens DeepState, la progression territoriale de l’armée russe en Ukraine s’est établie à 5 km² au cours du mois d’août, soit environ 0,16 km² d’avancée par jour en moyenne. Il s’agit du chiffre le plus bas depuis octobre 2023, lorsque Moscou avait mis fin à la contre-offensive de l’été, dans la région de Donetsk. La méthodologie utilisée par DeepState fournit une image imparfaite du ralentissement du rythme de l’armée russe. Le groupe est notamment dépendant des autorités ukrainiennes, qui peuvent chercher à retarder la communication de certaines informations afin de ne pas nuire à une opération en cours. Ainsi, en août, DeepState a attendu que le gouvernement communique sur les résultats de la contre-offensive lancée fin janvier pour les répercuter sur ses propres cartes, plutôt que de signaler au fil des opérations l’avancée réelle des forces ukrainiennes, provoquant ainsi un décalage artificiel. Selon l’analyste Clément Molin, les résultats d’une nouvelle contre-attaque dans le secteur de Lyman pourraient être annoncés dans les prochains jours. Celle-ci pourrait conduire à la récupération de 200 km² de territoire supplémentaire par Kiev Publication sur Telegram de Clément Molin , 30 août 2026.'> 2 . Malgré une chronologie parfois imprécise, la majorité des analystes s’accordent pour dire que l’armée russe ne parvient plus à avancer en Ukraine comme elle avait pu le faire depuis le début de l’année 2024. L'essoufflement des capacités offensives ainsi que la montée en puissance des forces ukrainiennes pourraient pousser Poutine à une nouvelle escalade. Selon une source proche du président russe, Poutine craint que mettre fin à la guerre sans avoir été en mesure de prendre le contrôle du Donbass pourrait sérieusement menacer son pouvoir – il aurait déclaré à un de ses proches : « Ils vont me pendre » Cornered, Vladimir Putin plans to escalate his war », The Economist , 30 août 2026.'> 3 . La visite le 25 août du directeur de la CIA à Moscou pourrait avoir constitué l’élément déclencheur de cette escalade : Poutine aurait en effet considéré celle-ci comme un signe de faiblesse de Trump, de la même manière qu’il avait interprété la visite de Bill Burns, en novembre 2021, comme un signe de faiblesse de Biden. Poutine pourrait notamment décider d’envoyer 300 à 400 000 soldats supplémentaires combattre sur le front, ce qui correspondrait à une hausse de 40 à 55 % par rapport aux forces russes déjà présentes en Ukraine, sans pour autant annoncer une nouvelle mobilisation. Selon des renseignements obtenus par les services ukrainiens, Moscou pourrait notamment chercher à lancer de nouveaux assauts en direction de Kiev et de Tchernihiv, une ville située à une cinquantaine de kilomètres de la frontière avec le Bélarus Збройні сили РФ отримали завдання спланувати операцію у напрямку Чернігова та Києва, — заступник керівника ОП Паліса », Суспільно , 29 août 2026.'> 4 . La dernière offensive russe sur cet axe remonte à 2022, dans le sillage de la tentative ratée de décapitation du pouvoir. L’article La progression russe en Ukraine est au plus bas depuis près de trois ans est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: FMI : un nouveau programme de 1 245 milliards de FCFA sur trois ans pour le Sénégal
items.description: Entre le Sénégal et le Fonds monétaire international (FMI), les négociations ont bien avancé. À l’issue de la mission entamée le 19 août dernier, un accord au niveau des services a été trouvé pour un partenariat technique d’une durée de trois ans. Il est adossé à un plan de décaissements du FMI d’un montant global de 2,2 milliards de dollars, soit environ 1 245 milliards de FCFA au taux de change de marché du 1er septembre 2026. L’information a été donnée par le représentant résident du FMI pour le Sénégal et auprès de la BCEAO, Majdi Debbich, en marge d’une interview exclusive accordée au Soleil. « C’est une première étape dans la mesure où cet accord au niveau des services doit maintenant être validé par notre Conseil d’administration. Mais c’est avant tout une étape importante qui vient couronner deux années de collaboration étroite que nous avons eue avec les autorités pour traiter à la fois la question du misreporting et des déclarations erronées sur la dette », a-t-il commenté. L’accord technique conclu entre les services du FMI et les autorités sénégalaises doit désormais être soumis à l’approbation du Conseil d’administration de l’institution. Sa validation constituera une étape déterminante avant la mise en œuvre du nouveau partenariat et les éventuels décaissements prévus dans ce cadre. Demba DIENG

items.title: Tebboune opère un remaniement ministériel : les 4 nouveaux ministres
items.description: Le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune , a opéré ce mardi un remaniement ministériel qui a touché quatre ministères, a annoncé la Présidence de la République dans un communiqué. Il a nommé le gouverneur de la Banque d’Algérie Mohamed Lamine Lebbou à la tête des Finances en remplacement d’Abdelkrim Bouzred. Le deuxième ministère concerné par ce remaniement est celui de l’Agriculture, du Développement rural et de la Pêche. Agriculture : Yacine Oualid cède sa place à Sid Ali Khaldi Yacine Oualid, qui a tenu une réunion ce mardi avec les cadres de son département autour des derniers incendies, est remplacé par l’avocat Sid Ali Khaldi, ancien ministre de la Jeunesse et des Sports (janvier 2020 – juillet 2021). Un autre ancien ministre de la Jeunesse et des Sports entre 2018 et 2019 revient au gouvernement. Il s’agit de Mohamed Hattab qui a été désigné à la tête du ministère du Travail, de la Protection sociale et de l’Emploi en remplacement de Abdelhak Saihi. Mohamed Hattab occupait depuis avril dernier le poste de médiateur de la République. Enfin, Mohamed Bouslimani, 69 ans, opère, lui aussi, son retour au gouvernement pour retrouver le ministère de la Communication qu’il avait dirigé de novembre 2021 à juin 2023. Il remplace Zoheir Bouamama qui ne boucle pas une année à la tête de ce ministère qu’il dirigeait depuis le 15 septembre 2025. Le changement à la tête de ce département survient deux semaines après le limogeage du secrétaire général Lyes Bouriche par le président de la République. L’article Tebboune opère un remaniement ministériel : les 4 nouveaux ministres est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Petite saison des pluies : Des précipitations normales à tendance excédentaire attendues dans le sud du Togo
items.description: Lomé, 1 er sept. (ATOP) – L’Agence nationale de la météorologie (ANAMET) a organisé, le mardi 1 er septembre à Lomé, une conférence de presse pour présenter les prévisions saisonnières des paramètres agro-hydro-climatiques de la petite saison des pluies dans le sud du Togo. Sur le plan cumuls pluviométriques, le sud du Togo connaîtra, au cours des mois de septembre, octobre et novembre, une situation pluviométrique normale à tendance excédentaire. Sur le plan agrométéorologique, il est prévu un démarrage tardif à normal de la saison agricole dans l’ensemble de la zone bimodale. Les dates de fin des saisons agricoles précoces devraient, quant à elles, rester normales dans les régions des Plateaux et Maritime. L’ANAMET prévoit également des séquences sèches longues à tendance normale en début de saison, tandis que les séquences sèches courtes devraient être à tendance normale vers la fin de la saison. Ces prévisions constituent un outil d’aide à la décision pour les producteurs, notamment dans la planification des opérations agricoles, le choix des périodes de semis et la gestion des ressources en eau. Sur le plan hydrologique, des écoulements normaux sont attendus sur l’ensemble des bassins du sud du pays. Une tendance excédentaire est toutefois prévue dans l’extrême nord-ouest du bassin de l’Oti. Face à ces perspectives, l’ANAMET recommande aux agriculteurs d’anticiper la préparation des sols et de procéder aux semis dès les premières pluies utiles. Elle conseille également de privilégier des variétés à cycle court, résilientes aux défis hydriques et à haut rendement. L’agence invite par ailleurs les populations à éviter l’occupation des zones inondables, aussi bien pour les habitations que pour les cultures. Elle préconise une gestion rationnelle des ressources en eau afin de répondre aux besoins des barrages hydroélectriques et des aménagements hydro-agricoles. Les producteurs sont également encouragés à prévoir l’irrigation de complément et à promouvoir des activités génératrices de revenus, particulièrement au profit des femmes et des jeunes. L’ANAMET recommande enfin aux usagers de suivre régulièrement les prévisions météorologiques quotidiennes et intra-saisonnières afin d’adapter les activités agricoles à l’évolution effective des conditions climatiques. Le directeur général de l’ANAMET, Dr Issaou Latifou, a souligné l’importance de l’information météorologique pour l’agriculture, secteur qui représente, selon lui, environ 70 de l’activité principale dans les pays concernés. « Les secteurs primaires, surtout les secteurs agricoles, représentent 70 à 75 % de l’activité phare au niveau de nos pays », a-t-il indiqué. Il a invité les producteurs à tenir compte des prévisions dans la planification de leurs activités, notamment face à une fin de saison précoce à normale, qui pourrait intervenir autour de la mi-novembre, voire dès le début du mois de novembre dans certaines zones. Les agriculteurs devront également se préparer aux longues séquences sèches en début de saison, susceptibles d’occasionner d’importantes pauses entre les épisodes pluvieux après les premiers semis. « Le démarrage de la saison va se faire d’une manière tardive », a-t-il précisé, appelant ainsi les producteurs à adapter le calendrier agricole aux conditions climatiques annoncées. Ces prévisions ont été présentées grâce à l’appui technique et financier du Programme de résilience du système alimentaire en Afrique de l’Ouest, projet-Togo (FSRP-Togo). ATOP/AO/SED

items.title: Occupation anarchique du domaine maritime : La phase de démolition et d’évacuation démarrée sur la côte togolaise
items.description: Lomé, 1 er sept. (ATOP) – Le comité ad’hoc de lutte contre l’occupation anarchique du domaine public dans le Grand Lomé et les communes des Lacs, a démarré, le mardi 1 er septembre à Lomé, la phase de démolition et d’enlèvement des installations irrégulières pour libérer, sécuriser et préserver le littoral du Togo. Des occupants en train de récupérer leurs installations Cette étape décisive fait suite au point de presse animé par la présidente du Comité ad’hoc et gouverneur du District autonome du Grand Lomé (DAGL), Mme Zouréhatou Kassah-Traoré, le 31 juillet dernier à Lomé. Au cours de cette séance, le chronogramme des opérations d’intérêt général avait été dévoilé. L’objectif de la démarche est de restaurer la vocation publique des plages, garantir un libre accès à tous les usagers et mettre un terme définitif aux appropriations privées illégales, tout en répondant aux urgences sécuritaires et environnementales. Pour mener à bien ce processus, les autorités avaient procédé le 27 juillet dernier à un marquage rigoureux des infrastructures devant être démontées. Un délai de grâce d’un mois (août) avait été accordé aux occupants et exploitants afin qu’ils libèrent eux-mêmes les espaces et remettent les sites en l’état. L’opération qui a débuté de la frontière du quartier de Kodjoviakopé jusqu’au niveau de l’hôtel Palm Beach, a consisté à la démolition et l’évacuation des matériaux et des déchets accumulés. Des mécanismes de surveillance et de sécurisation sont également déployés pour prévenir toute réinstallation clandestine sur le domaine maritime. Dans une déclaration rendue public le 31 août, le comité ad’hoc a tenu à rappeler une règle juridique fondamentale, le domaine public maritime relève de la compétence exclusive de l’État central. Aucune autorité locale ni individu ne peut s’en arroger la gestion ou la cession. Le comité invite l’ensemble des acteurs riverains, collectivités territoriales, commerçants, professionnels du secteur et médias à faire preuve de civisme et de responsabilité pour soutenir cette salubrité publique. Le comité a réaffirmé sa détermination à conduire ces opérations dans un esprit de transparence, de coordination et de rigueur. ATOP/SED/HKM/BV
